articles.content: So, what'd I miss? It's been quite a buzzing start to the week but today, it seems that markets might settle for doing nothing - at least in European morning trade. The US inflation data is looming later and I suspect European traders might be more than happy to sit on their hands until then. US CPI day means that the inflation numbers will be the main event for markets. As such, I wouldn't expect much excitement in the hours to follow as traders keep their powder dry ahead of the release; that unless we get some surprise headlines during the session. The October report is expected to show headline inflation rising by 0.3% m/m, easing from 0.6% in September. Meanwhile, core inflation is estimated to slow to 0.2% m/m, down from 0.3% previously. Just be wary though that there is an important caveat to the release this time around. The BLS will not be publishing the usual annual comparisons for today's report, owing to missing October 2025 data during the government shutdown last year. As such, that puts even more emphasis on the monthly readings. The bigger question later today is whether the numbers will give markets another reason to feel better about themselves, especially after tech shares have rebounded quite well since the selloff last week. The Nasdaq gained another 2.7% yesterday while the S&P 500 climbed by 2.3% as risk appetite recovered alongside a sharp decline in oil prices. Even though tech shares have found their footing again, concerns surrounding AI spending and potential regulatory hurdles haven't exactly disappeared. As such, today's inflation report might be one to help tip the balance of scales in that regard. A softer report could offer some welcome relief for equities, particularly if it helps temper expectations for another Fed rate hike in December. Meanwhile, a hotter print risks throwing another spanner in the works considering that the recent recovery is still finding its legs. Hotter inflation could spark Treasury yields to nudge higher again and weigh on the already expensive tech valuations further. But for now, I suspect traders will be reluctant to chase the rebound too aggressively before getting a clearer inflation signal. In any case, Europe will be facing a quieter session in the day ahead with the real fireworks reserved for the US data later today. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

Vaiana Express releases a guide helping shoppers decide if a traditional watch suits an Apple Watch owner, covering style, wearing habits, and movement types like quartz, Eco-Drive, and automatic. Staten Island, United States, November 9, 2026 -- Vaiana Express has released a guide for people deciding whether to give a traditional watch to someone who already wears an Apple Watch. The guide addresses whether the gift makes sense and, if so, how to pick a watch that matches the recipient's style and daily habits, since gift-givers can struggle to judge whether a second watch would be worn regularly or left in a drawer. https://vaianaexpress.com/blogs/news/traditional-watch-gift-for-apple-watch-wearer According to the guide, a traditional watch does not need to take over the duties an Apple Watch already handles. Instead, it can fill a separate role for dinners, weddings, weekend outings, or any stretch of time when notifications are unwelcome, which means the new watch and the smartwatch are not competing for the same wrist time. The guide encourages gift-givers to look for signs that the recipient would welcome this kind of addition before buying one, such as admiring a particular dial, dressing up deliberately for events, or mentioning a wish to step away from notifications. When those signs are absent, the guide suggests simply asking whether the person would enjoy a separate watch for dinners or special occasions, rather than guessing. Once interest is established, the guide turns to a less obvious decision: matching the watch's movement to how often it will actually be worn. Quartz watches are generally easy to pick up again after days of disuse, while light-powered models need periodic exposure to keep their charge, and automatic watches may stop running when left idle, requiring the owner to wind and reset them, a routine some wearers enjoy and others would rather avoid. To make these distinctions concrete, the guide walks through four specific watches drawn from the Citizen, Tissot, Seiko, and Movado collections. Case sizes range from 28 mm to 44 mm across the group, with each example pairing a movement type with a particular occasion, from a low-maintenance Eco-Drive model to a dress watch meant for formal evenings. Taken together, the guide gives shoppers a structured way to weigh style, size, and upkeep before committing to a gift. Vaiana Express sources its watches, including Swiss automatic models and brands such as TAG Heuer, Movado, Michael Kors, and Emporio Armani, through authorized dealer relationships, and supports purchases with US shipping and customer support. articles.title: Jordon Hudson sues Airbnb hosts, blaming them for shirtless Bill Belichick video
articles.desc: Airbnb hosts violated the privacy of Bill Belichick’s former girlfriend Jordon Hudson by leaking doorbell video of her shirtless, Super Bowl-winning boyfriend.
articles.content: Jordon Hudson sues Airbnb hosts, blaming them for shirtless Bill Belichick video IE 11 is not supported. For an optimal experience visit our site on another browser. Airbnb hosts violated the privacy of Bill Belichick’s former girlfriend by leaking unflattering doorbell video of her shirtless, Super Bowl-winning boyfriend three years ago, according to a lawsuit she filed Friday in Massachusetts civil court. Jordon Hudson claimed that hosts Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan “exhibited no remorse or regard for these” actions taken outside the defendants’ Airbnb home in Winthrop. Hudson, now 25, and Belichick, 74, had wanted to keep their May-December romance under wraps when they checked in to the defendants’ home for a four-night stay at 27 Brewster Ave. in summer 2023, the lawsuit said. During the final night of the getaway, McDevitt texted Hudson asking her not to park in front of their neighbor’s home. The message also included “a link to a Ring video of a shirtless Mr. Belichick walking to and from the Property, which had been captured and saved without the knowledge and authorization of Mr. Belichick or Ms. Hudson,” according to the lawsuit, which was filed Friday Hudson claimed that McDevitt agreed to delete the video, only for it to hit social media later in the year, making Hudson’s relationship with Belichick known to the public. McDevitt then reached out to Hudson, “out of the blue,” according to the lawsuit, in May 2025 and admitted having shared the video with friends, according to the civil complaint. “We had sent it to a few people initially wondering is this him [Mr. Belichick], isn’t it him and I don’t know what happened from there, but we did delete it from the camera, as I assured you,” McDevitt is alleged to have written to Hudson, according to the lawsuit. Hudson didn’t name a dollar amount she’s seeking. McDevitt and Nolan couldn’t immediately be reached for comment Monday at publicly listed phone numbers and email addresses. Representatives of Belichick, Ring and Airbnb, none of whom are named parties to the civil action, also couldn’t be reached for comment Monday. Boston civil attorney Michael Coyne said he doesn’t believe Hudson has any claim for damages because she and Belichick had no expectation of privacy outside the Airbnb home. articles.desc: A 42-year-old man, who was charged with the offence of riot last year in Ballymena, has been jailed.
articles.content: Jail term for Ballymena rioter (42) who was identified after he removed balaclava Jail term for Ballymena rioter (42) who was identified after he removed balaclava A 42-year-old man, who was charged with the offence of riot last year in Ballymena, has been jailed. William Wylie, with an address listed as Orkney Drive, Ballymena, was sentenced to 28 months, with half to be served in custody, and half on licence. On Monday, June 9, 2025 large-scale disorder broke out on the streets of Ballymena, involving a crowd of rioters and lasting for three consecutive nights. Further violence occurred across Northern Ireland. There was disorder at Harryville Bridge, Bridge Street Ballymena, on June 10, 2025. A large crowd, some wearing face coverings/balaclavas, were recorded on various forms of footage, throwing bottles and masonry at Police lines. Sign up for a free Northern Ireland World newsletter and let us bring the news to you Wylie’s image was shared to the public and police say he was identified as being involved in rioting on June 10, 2025. He was identified when he removed a balaclava and also by a tattoo, which was visible on the back of his right hand. He was arrested on September 1, 2025. Speaking after the sentencing at Antrim Crown Court on Friday (November 6), Detective Chief Inspector O'Loan said: “In shameful scenes, there was large-scale disorder by people intent on causing harm. Damage was caused to roads, homes, cars and local business premises with people left fearing for their lives. “Our officers came under attack and many left injured after petrol bombs, heavy masonry and fireworks were thrown at them. “Our dedicated investigation team has worked tirelessly to ensure that those involved are prosecuted – today’s sentencing is one of many over this disorder.” Iconic Media Group Ltd. articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair in staff memo as board opens investigation
articles.desc: In a written memo to employees on Sunday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he had been unfaithful to his wife. He sent it after news reports tied him to Alice Huang, an AI executive the reports describe as a suspected Chinese spy. On the same day, Nvidia's Board of Directors said it was investigating Hu
articles.content: In a written memo to employees on Sunday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he had been unfaithful to his wife. He sent it after news reports tied him to Alice Huang, an AI executive the reports describe as a suspected Chinese spy. On the same day, Nvidia's Board of Directors said it was investigating Huang's relationship with Alice Huang. They have the same surname, and the source material doesn't say whether they're related. What the board is investigating The investigation is about the national security concerns that news reports raised over the relationship. Huang wrote that the board has "initiated an independent investigation" and said he will "cooperate fully." Alice Huang isn't named anywhere in the memo, and Huang doesn't respond to the spy allegations head-on. His only reference to them is the phrase "the national security concerns raised in news reports." Most of the memo is an apology, first to his family and then to employees, the board, partners and shareholders. The memo in full This is the complete text Nvidia employees received: To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. The memo was signed "Jensen." What the memo leaves out Huang wrote that he is "fully committed to NVIDIA" and will "work to earn back your confidence," which suggests he intends to stay in the job while the investigation goes on. The memo has no timeline for the investigation. It doesn't say who is running it, or whether the findings will be released publicly. He ends by asking for privacy for his family, who he said "bears no responsibility for my choices."

In a vote of confidence that will resound throughout Canada’s auto manufacturing business, Honda just announced that its Alliston, Ontario plants will be re-tooling to produce the next generation of hybrid- and gasoline-powered Civics and CR-Vs. More importantly, Honda of Canada Manufacturing will be “maintaining its workforce of more than 4,000 Canadians” at least for the near- and mid-term future, a huge commitment by the Japanese giant considering the pressure being exerted by the Trump administration to move those jobs south of the border. “For 40 years, Honda associates in Alliston have demonstrated the skill, innovation, and commitment that have made our Canadian operations a cornerstone of Honda’s manufacturing network in North America,” said Dave Jamieson, President and CEO of Honda Canada Inc. “It [also] reflects the dedication of our more than 4,000 associates and will generate lasting benefits for our suppliers, local communities, and the broader Canadian economy.” We apologize, but this video has failed to load. tap here to see other videos from our team We apologize, but this video has failed to load. tap here to see other videos from our team It’s worth noting that Jamieson’s words carry some weight because, unlike some other automakers — notably the Detroit Three — Honda has laid off a full-time assembly-line worker in its 40 years in Canada. According to Honda, this is all part of the company’s investment of $867 million in Canada over the near-term future, of which $313 million will come from the federal government; and another $156 million from Ontario. According to Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, this was all part of the province’s “plan to protect workers and businesses impacted by U.S. tariffs and fortify our industrial base” while Vic Fedeli, Ontario’s Minister of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade, said that “this retooling [will] enhance Alliston’s operations… further anchoring Ontario workers at the heart of their North American supply chain.” Honda produced some 401,000 vehicles in Canada last year — more than all that the Detroit Three made here in 2025 — and has assembled more than 11 million vehicles in Canada since 1996. articles.title: 1998 KY26: Here’s What We Know About The Mysterious Dark Comet Soon To Be Visited By JAXA’s Hayabusa2
articles.desc: The Japanese reconnaissance probe will arrive at KY26 by 2031
articles.content: 1998 KY26: Here’s What We Know About The Mysterious Dark Comet Soon To Be Visited By JAXA’s Hayabusa2 1998 KY26: Here’s What We Know About The Mysterious Dark Comet Soon To Be Visited By JAXA’s Hayabusa2 The Japanese reconnaissance probe will arrive at KY26 by 2031 Dutch-American astronomer Tom Gehrels found 1998 KY26 on 28 May 1998 at Spacewatch in Arizona. It was making a close pass by Earth at the time. In 1998 it was timed at 10.7 minutes per spin, a record then. Further observation in 2024 halved that to 5.35 minutes. Its albedo is 0.52. Radar readings in 1998 showed a width of about 30 meters. However, the observations in 2024 sliced the width to 11 meters, which is about the length of a telephone pole and roughly Hayabusa2's own size. Relatively, the other astroid Ryugu is about 82 times bigger, which the probe will also visit. Astronomers have listed it as a dark comet since 2023. Its orbit gets pushed the way a comet does, but there is no coma and no tail. Nobody knows why. Is there outgassing that we can't detect yet? JAXA picked KY26 as the final target of Hayabusa2's extended mission in September 2020. A flyby of asteroid Torifune came first, in July 2026. Arrival at KY26 is set for July 2031. 2026 ED138: Rubin Observatory Finds Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Neptune [In Pics] If confirmed, ED138 would join the five dwarf planets recognized by the International Astronomical Union: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake.
